scope: Ground vehicle danger point-suppression qualification; direct target fire unchanged
finding: Danger point suppression used general damaging-ammunition readiness without selecting or acknowledging the qualified muzzle. It bypassed routine speed/range/terrain/current-engagement guards.
change: Ground danger point suppression now requires nonexplosive shotBullet with at least20 loaded rounds, >=50m separation, speed<30km/h, terrain clearance, no current suppression/unrelated native engagement, existing target hold and selected-muzzle acknowledgement. Eight-second hold starts only on issued suppression.
intent: Use bounded native suppression without competing movement, arbitrary explosive fire or overriding an existing engagement. Direct identified-target and combined ground fire retain target-qualified ammunition choices.
departures: No delayed random UseWeapon shot from upstream.
No forced movement, projectile changes or new controller.
Air branch retains existing policy; this is not air-suppression acceptance.
limits: Protected-person cone is not blast/geometry proof.
Native muzzle selection and actual firing/effect remain physically unverified.
Runtime overhead unmeasured; one bounded station scan only after cheap danger gates.
